ApertureA snapshot of public health data. Open the scope to regions and states, or close it to counties and cities.
    Loading data for 3,100+ counties…
    About the data. Each row shows its data year and source. Different sources cover different years, so read each measure on its own terms.
    CDC PLACES models county estimates from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System survey. Values are age-adjusted so counties with older or younger populations can be compared fairly. The latest values come from the 2025 release (mostly 2023 survey data). Kentucky and Pennsylvania were not in the 2025 release, so their values come from the 2024 release. PLACES trends combine five releases (2021–2025). CDC cautions that model changes between releases mean small differences may not reflect real change. The colorectal screening age range changed from 50–75 to 45–75 in the 2024 release. Connecticut switched to 9 planning regions in 2024, so its trends start in 2022.
    County Health Rankings & Roadmaps (University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute) supplies life expectancy, premature death, infant and child deaths, low birthweight, provider counts, preventable hospital stays, flu shots, housing, food, income and other community measures. Where the March 2026 supplemental release updated a measure, the page uses it. Otherwise it uses the 2025 release. Trend lines for these measures come from the CHR&R trends file, and the year shown is the last year of each data window.
    Causes of death. Heart disease and stroke death rates come from the CDC Interactive Atlas of Heart Disease and Stroke (adults 35+, age-adjusted, spatially smoothed, 2022–2024). Overdose, suicide, homicide and firearm death rates come from CDC’s Mapping Injury, Overdose, and Violence county data (2019–2024). Rates for counties with 1–9 deaths are suppressed. Air pollution is CDC’s modeled daily PM2.5, averaged over each year and weighted by population. EPA’s annual health standard is 9.0 µg/m³.
    From HealthData.gov. COVID-19 totals come from the HHS COVID-19 Community Profile Report (county level, final edition of May 10, 2023). Deaths are divided by the county’s current population. Medicare measures come from the CMS Medicare Geographic Variation file (2014–2024), which covers Original (fee-for-service) Medicare only, so counties where most people use Medicare Advantage are described by a smaller group. Hospital counts and star ratings come from the CMS Hospital General Information file (July 2026), matched to counties by name. Both CMS files are listed in the HealthData.gov catalog.
    Cities, states and regions. Cities are the 2,300+ places with at least 20,000 residents in CDC PLACES. They have PLACES health estimates and Census community measures, since the other sources report by county. State values use official state figures from County Health Rankings and CMS where published. Otherwise they are population-weighted averages of county estimates, shown only when counties covering at least half the state’s population have data. Regions are population-weighted averages of their states. Census regions and divisions follow the U.S. Census Bureau. The popular regions are common groupings: West Coast (CA, OR, WA), Pacific Northwest (WA, OR, ID), Mountain West (ID, MT, WY, CO, UT, NV), Southwest (AZ, NM, NV, UT), Great Lakes (IL, IN, MI, MN, OH, WI), Great Plains (KS, NE, ND, SD, OK), Mid-Atlantic (NY, NJ, PA, DE, MD, DC), Southeast (AL, AR, FL, GA, KY, LA, MS, NC, SC, TN, VA, WV) and Deep South (AL, GA, LA, MS, SC).
    US average uses the official national value where the source publishes one. Otherwise it is the population-weighted average of county values. “About the same” means the US average falls inside the county estimate’s 95% confidence interval (PLACES measures only).
    Sources: CDC PLACES county data (2021–2025 releases) · CDC PLACES place (city) data (2021–2025 releases) · CDC Non-Medical Factor Measures for Place · CDC Non-Medical Factor Measures, ACS 2017–2021 · County Health Rankings & Roadmaps 2025 data and March 2026 supplement · CDC Heart Disease Mortality 2022–2024 · CDC Stroke Mortality 2022–2024 · CDC Mapping Injury, Overdose, and Violence · CDC Daily County-Level PM2.5, 2001–2022 · HHS COVID-19 Community Profile Report, County-Level (HealthData.gov) · CMS Medicare Geographic Variation by National, State & County (HealthData.gov) · CMS Hospital General Information (HealthData.gov) · County boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau (2023), via us-atlas.
